Incident: N-able N-central authentication bypass exploitation (CVE-2026-18577 / incomplete fix of CVE-2026-18556)
Access path: Unauthenticated authentication bypass on internet-facing N-central servers, giving admin control. Attackers then used N-central Take Control to reach managed devices and installed Cloudflare Tunnel and other RMM tools for persistence.
Orgs reached (as reported): 'A limited number of customers' impacted, no count given (N-able, Aug 2026); one compromised organisation observed, 'no evidence that compromises are widespread' (Sophos CTU, Aug 2026)
Coding notes: MSP-relevant, not MSP-specific: no primary source names an MSP victim. N-able says managed devices were reached via Take Control, but not that they belonged to an MSP's customers, so boundary NR. Lateral movement: Sophos saw N-central used to reach DCs and a backup server, technique undescribed. PhantomKiller killed Sophos scanner. ACSC advisory unreachable.
People or orgs exposed: Limited number of N-able customers, uncounted (N-able, 10 Aug 2026); 1 organisation (Sophos, Aug 2026)

Incident: Bomgar / BeyondTrust Remote Support CVE-2026-1731 exploitation at an MSP and a dental software company, reaching downstream customers
Access path: Likely exploitation of CVE-2026-1731 (pre-auth OS command injection) on outdated self-hosted Bomgar/BeyondTrust Remote Support instances. At the MSP a high-privilege MSP Bomgar account was used to push remote access tools to a domain controller, giving reach into downstream client environments. At the dental software vendor, ransomware was deployed from its compromised Bomgar instance to downstream companies.
Orgs reached (as reported): MSP: 4 downstream customers exploited, after 'mass isolation of 78 businesses'; dental software company: 3 downstream companies hit by ransomware (Huntress, 17 Apr 2026). 7 downstream orgs plus the 2 providers.
Coding notes: Huntress says the root cause 'likely' is CVE-2026-1731 but is unconfirmed. Coded only the MSP (Apr 15) and dental (Apr 14) cases. Driver-based EDR killing (Apr 12) and the Atera scheduled task (Apr 3) were other victims, so excluded. Who isolated the 78 businesses is unclear. Trust boundary could be 'RMM or management platform' (Huntress calls Bomgar an RMM).

Incident: HIQ (Boston-area managed IT provider) Quest KACE SMA appliance compromise
Access path: Likely exploitation of CVE-2025-32975 (authentication bypass in KACE SMA SSO handling) on HIQ's unpatched, internet-facing KACE SMA. HIQ used it to manage endpoints for its client organisations. The exploit chain against HIQ was not shown and is inferred.
Orgs reached (as reported): HIQ, plus data on more than 60 named client organisations whose endpoints were managed through the compromised KACE SMA instance, found in the exfiltrated database (Hunt.io, May 2026). Compromise of client endpoints was not confirmed. Hardcoded credentials also show at least one unrelated environment (BRI Insurance, Indonesia) was compromised in the same campaign.
Coding notes: Single threat-intel source. The attacker's open directory held sql.zip, a 512 MB MariaDB dump of the KACE SMA: accounts, unsalted SHA-1 hashes, encrypted passwords, endpoint inventory, client list, tickets. Reverse shell, kace_admin account script, SMB sprayer and tunnels were staged, not confirmed run, so NR. The '60+ endpoints accessed' claim in the conclusion overstates the body. Publication date: May 12, but page metadata says Nov 2026.

Incident: Mimecast certificate compromise (SolarWinds/SUNBURST actor; M365 Exchange Web Services certificate)
Access path: SUNBURST backdoor in Mimecast's own SolarWinds Orion install; lateral movement to production grid servers; theft of a Mimecast-issued certificate authenticating Sync and Recover, Continuity Monitor and IEP to M365 EWS, plus encrypted customer service-account credentials; Microsoft reported the certificate was used to connect to a low single-digit number of customer M365 tenants from non-Mimecast IPs
Orgs reached (as reported): Low single-digit number of customers' M365 tenants targeted (Mimecast, 12 Jan 2021; restated 16 Mar 2021). About 10% of customers used the affected connection. Encrypted service-account credentials of US- and UK-hosted customers were accessed and potentially exfiltrated, number unstated (Mimecast, 26 Jan 2021)
Coding notes: Mimecast is an email-security SaaS vendor, not an MSP, so coded MSP-relevant. Trust boundary could arguably be API credential or token. Lateral movement occurred inside Mimecast only, not into customers, so capability is NR and behaviour is Y. March report (now 404) read via secondary quotes: source code and contact data accessed; no evidence email or archive content was accessed. Exfiltration Y rests on downloaded source code.
People or orgs exposed: Low single-digit number of customer M365 tenants targeted (Mimecast, 16 Mar 2021); credentials of an unstated number of US/UK-hosted customers exposed (Mimecast, 26 Jan 2021)

Incident: JumpCloud commands framework abused by a DPRK nation-state actor (UNC4899/TraderTraitor; CrowdStrike: North Korea)
Access path: Spear-phishing of JumpCloud staff (22 Jun 2023), then access to an internal orchestration system and data injection into the JumpCloud commands framework. The JumpCloud agent on customer devices then ran a malicious Ruby script (init.rb) that downloaded and ran second-stage macOS backdoors.
Orgs reached (as reported): Fewer than 5 JumpCloud customers and fewer than 10 devices in total (JumpCloud CISO Bob Phan; repeated by Mandiant, which investigated one affected customer with 4 macOS systems targeted)
Coding notes: Customer devices ran the Ruby script through the agent (T1059/T1072), the second-stage payloads (FULLHOUSE.DOORED, STRATOFEAR, TIEDYE) were downloaded, and persistence came from LaunchDaemon plists. Keychain targeting is Mandiant's general description of the actor, not an observation, so it is NR. Boundary crossed because several customers were reached, not because data was exposed. Identity provider was considered as the trust boundary, but the abused component was device management (commands).
People or orgs exposed: Fewer than 5 customer organisations / fewer than 10 devices (JumpCloud, figure cited by Mandiant 24 Jul 2023)

Incident: TietoEVRY ransomware attack on Norwegian hosted infrastructure disrupting services for 25 customers
Orgs reached (as reported): 25 customers (retail, manufacturing, service industries), per TietoEVRY statement 23 Feb 2021
Coding notes: I found no December 2021 Norway incident. The matching event is February 2021, disclosed 23 Feb 2021. The primary URL now redirects, so I read its text through a seclists.org mirror. No techniques, ransomware family or data exposure were reported. Tier 2 follows the shared-hosting ransomware convention.

Access path: Ransomware on Ingram Micro internal systems. Unnamed sources told BleepingComputer the attackers got in through the GlobalProtect VPN, likely with stolen credentials; Palo Alto said its products were not the cause. Ingram Micro took systems offline, and its Xvantage ordering and Impulse licence-provisioning services went down for customers in many countries.
Orgs reached (as reported): No customer count published. Ingram Micro (5 Jul 2025 release) describes a system outage that disrupted order processing and shipping for 'customers, vendor partners, and others' worldwide. Operations restored in all regions by about 9 Jul 2025.
Coding notes: Tier 2 follows the shared-hosting ransomware convention. Crossed boundary and Multiple tenants are Y only under the multi-customer-outage convention; confirmed stolen data covers employees and applicants, not customers. VPN and credential access rest on unnamed sources. SafePay's 3.5 TB claim is unverified. Maine and Mass. notices returned 403; their content comes from search snippets and coverage.
People or orgs exposed: 42,521 individuals (employees and job applicants), per Maine AG notice; consumers notified 16 Jan 2026

Access path: Zero-day exploitation of internet-facing on-premises VSA servers (authentication bypass, SQL injection in userFilterTableRpt.asp, arbitrary file upload); attackers then pushed a malicious 'Kaseya VSA Agent Hot-fix' procedure through VSA agents to MSP-managed customer endpoints
Orgs reached (as reported): Fewer than 60 direct Kaseya customers (all VSA on-premises, mostly MSPs) and fewer than 1,500 downstream businesses (Kaseya, July 2021); Huntress tracked about 30 MSPs and well over 1,000 encrypted businesses
Coding notes: Account modification: Huntress saw a KElevated SQL account disable VSA admin accounts. Sophos explicitly says there was no shadow-copy deletion and no apparent exfiltration attempt, hence N. The 'Archive and Purge Logs' procedure deleted logs; it was not data archiving. REvil claimed about 1M devices, which was not confirmed. Credential exposure in CVE-2021-30116 is a CVE description only, so NR.
People or orgs exposed: Fewer than 1,500 downstream businesses and fewer than 60 direct customers (Kaseya, July 2021)

Incident: Atento (customer-service / BPO provider) cyberattack on Brazil operations, October 2021
Orgs reached (as reported): Unspecified number of Brazilian clients whose services were interrupted ('some customers', 6-K 22 Oct 2021; 'certain clients', 20-F FY2021 auditor CAM); Atento says attack did not reach client systems
Coding notes: Ransomware coded Y because the 20-F says Atento paid no ransom and describes cleaning servers at every site. Encryption and the LockBit attribution and data leak come only from news (Canaltech), so Data exposed and Exfiltration are NR. Customer boundary is N because the Q3 report says the attack was prevented from reaching client systems. Atento is a BPO, not an IT provider, so General supply-chain. Losses: $34.8M revenue plus $11.3M costs.

Incident: Cisco Duo third-party telephony (SMS/VoIP MFA) provider breach
Access path: Attacker phished a provider employee's credentials and used them on 1 Apr 2024 to get into the unnamed telephony provider's internal systems. From there they downloaded the SMS MFA message logs (phone number, carrier, country, state, date/time, message type) for messages sent to users across Duo customer accounts between 1 and 31 Mar 2024.
Orgs reached (as reported): Not disclosed by Cisco. Cisco notified multiple Duo customer accounts. Press estimate of about 1,000 notified customers is unconfirmed.
Coding notes: Only primary source is Cisco's 15 Apr 2024 customer notice. Its link no longer loads; text verified via SecurityWeek and The Record. Access credentials N: provider explicitly said message content (passcodes) was not accessed and no messages sent. Phished employee credentials were T1566, not T1003/T1552. Duo itself was not compromised, so General supply-chain.
People or orgs exposed: NR (Cisco gave no count of users or customer accounts; ~1,000 customers is an unconfirmed press estimate, Apr 2024)

Incident: Swiss Cloud Computing AG hosting provider ransomware
Access path: NR (not disclosed; company reportedly attributed the infection to a breach of an internal company-wide directive)
Orgs reached (as reported): About 6,500 end customers whose hosted services were disrupted (Swiss Cloud Computing statement, reported by netzwoche/itreseller, April 2021); hosted Sage, Europa3000 and Buspro applications were affected
Coding notes: Status page: cyberattack from 27 Apr 2021; no data outflow per current knowledge (30 Apr, 5 May); backups usable for recovery. MedusaLocker and 'no ransom paid' come only from company statements relayed by netzwoche, not the status page. Crossed boundary and Exfiltration coded N on company's hedged denial. myBACKUP service outage counted as disruption, not alteration.
People or orgs exposed: None reported (Swiss Cloud status page: no signs customer data leaked, 5 May 2021)

Incident: AOMEI Backupper update infrastructure tampering (UNC7017, CROSSROAD/SHINYROAD)
Access path: For 5 to 10 minutes at a time, UNC7017 changed AOMEI's remote update and notification config files (down_html.ini, Notifycfg.ini) on aomeisoftware.com. The files were not authenticated. The changes sent polling Backupper clients to an attacker archive containing the CROSSROAD dropper and made the client run it locally. A 20 Jul change added a hidden UNC/WebDAV popup to force NTLM authentication. How the attacker got onto the server has not been reported.
Orgs reached (as reported): No count given. GTIG/Mandiant: impacted organisations in IT services, telecoms and higher education across 11 countries, likely an undercount. ManageEngine METAL: 2 endpoints in 2 unrelated organisations on 28 May 2026.
Coding notes: Disclosed 15-16 Oct 2026. Access credentials=Y from observed NTLM coercion; harvested hashes are unconfirmed (AOMEI says 'may'), and forced authentication falls outside T1003/T1552, so the behaviour is NR. SHINYROAD shell is malware design; Shell=Y rests on observed hidden-PowerShell task. Products are consumer/SMB backup tools, not MSP tooling, so General; MSP-relevant is arguable. Eleven countries implies at least 11 orgs.

Incident: Inline Network Integration (Texas MSP) breach of client data hosted on its network
Orgs reached (as reported): Number of customers not stated; Inline's template letter says the actor 'may have acquired some Inline customer data including <<Inline Customer Name>> data' (CA AG). Only Heritage Life Insurance Co. is named in public filings (CA AG; Indiana AG).
Coding notes: Inline's letter says it is the 'MSP' and client data was 'hosted on Inline's network'. The 'Ransomware at IT services vendor' cause comes from the Maine AG listing, seen only in a search-index snippet because the page blocked fetching. Exfiltration is NR because the letter only says the actor 'may have acquired' data. The 58,144 figure covers Heritage Life only. No techniques are reported.
People or orgs exposed: 58,144 individuals (Heritage Life Insurance Co. notice to Indiana AG, sent 7/14/2022); total across all Inline customers not reported
